title: Smooth finite-field model of a prescribed geometric closed curve
statement: Fix $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, its algebraic closure $k$, and the subfields $k_m=\mathbf F_{q^m}\subset k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $X_0$ be an affine finite-type $k_0$-scheme and put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum; def-weil-finite-type-morphism; def-pc-base-change]. Let $i:C\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], where $C$ is a nonempty smooth connected affine $k$-scheme of pure dimension one [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms; def-weil-connected-scheme; def-weil-pure-dimension]. There exist $m\ge1$, an affine finite-type $k_m$-scheme $C_m$, a closed immersion $i_m:C_m\hookrightarrow X_0\times_{k_0}k_m$, and an isomorphism $(C_m)_k\simeq C$ commuting with the immersions into $X$. The scheme $C_m$ is smooth, geometrically connected [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], and of pure dimension one. Moreover, for every given $k$-point $c$ of $C$, its image $z$ in $C_m$ is a closed point and $\kappa(z)/k_m$ is finite. The same model works for any prescribed finite set of such points, without enlarging the field separately for each point.

proof.text: Apply [lem-zl-bertini-finite-field-descent] to the given closed immersion. It supplies one integer $m\ge1$ and a closed subscheme $i_m:C_m\hookrightarrow X_m=X_0\times_{k_0}k_m$ whose base change is the prescribed closed subscheme $i:C\hookrightarrow X$. Equality as closed subschemes supplies the required isomorphism $(C_m)_k\simeq C$ over $X$, including its compatibility with the given immersion; no reduction of the subscheme is taken.

source.place: Paragraph 2: finite-field model of the prescribed geometric curve, and closed points under its geometric lifts (old steps 2-3 and end of 4).

proof.text: The ambient model is affine by the affine base-change instances. The closed immersion i_m is affine and locally of finite type by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Hence its source C_m is affine. Its structure morphism is the composite of i_m with the base change of X_0 to k_m, so it is locally of finite type and quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. No tensor-product presentation of the ambient model is needed.

The map $g:\operatorname{Spec}k\to\operatorname{Spec}k_m$ is flat by [lem-pc-field-extension-flat]. Both spectra have one point by [def-weil-affine-spectrum], so $g$ is surjective and quasi-compact: the inverse image of either open of the target is empty or a one-point space. Thus $g$ meets all three hypotheses of fpqc smoothness descent. Moreover [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] applied to $g$ and $C_m\to\operatorname{Spec}k_m$ makes the projection $p:C\simeq(C_m)_k\to C_m$ surjective. In particular $C_m$ is nonempty.

source.place: Tag 02VL (lemma-descending-property-smooth), verification of the single fpqc base change

proof.text: The base change of $C_m\to\operatorname{Spec}k_m$ along $g$ is $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, which is smooth by hypothesis. Apply [lem-trf-smooth-fpqc-base-descent], with the flat, quasi-compact, surjective map $g$ verified in step 3, to obtain smoothness of $C_m$. The field $k$ is algebraically closed and contains $k_m$; the connectedness of $(C_m)_k\simeq C$ therefore gives geometric connectedness of $C_m$ by [lem-weil-geometrically-connected-algebraic-closure]. Neither argument requires another constant extension.

Apply the proved scheme-level theorem [lem-sbc-equidimensional-open-local-dimension] to the top open of C. The given pure-dimension hypothesis, transported along the homeomorphism between C and its top open, yields local dimension one at each point of C. Lift each point of C_m to its geometric base change using the surjective projection from step 3, and then to C using the comparison isomorphism. Homeomorphism invariance of local topological dimension and the local-dimension equality of [lem-trf-field-extension-component-local-dimension] give local dimension one at every point of C_m. The model is locally Noetherian because it is locally of finite type over a field. Apply the proved top-open instance of [lem-sbc-constant-local-dimension-components] and transport its component dimensions along the top-open homeomorphism. This proves exactly [def-weil-pure-dimension] for C_m, without another field extension.

Let $c:\operatorname{Spec}k\to C$ be any given $k$-point, and let $z$ be the image of its composite with $p$. The residue-field map of [def-weil-residue-field] is an embedding $\kappa(z)\hookrightarrow k$ over $k_m$. Every element of $k$ is algebraic over $k_0$, hence also over $k_m$, so $\kappa(z)/k_m$ is algebraic and has transcendence degree zero. Since $C_m$ is of finite type over $k_m$, clause (a) of [lem-kun-closed-point-field] now says both that $z$ is closed and that $\kappa(z)/k_m$ is finite.

source.place: Clause (a), applied to the already constructed finite-type model

proof.text: The integer $m$ and the model in step 1 were chosen before any point was considered. Step 6 applies to each $k$-point individually for that fixed model. Applying this universal assertion to every member of any prescribed finite set proves the simultaneous assertion, including the empty finite set, with exactly the same $m$, $C_m$, and immersion.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q42-7d1a79a7a (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item in full; this delivery adds no new nodes. The statement is unchanged and only gains three existing definition stmt_deps. All seven steps check out. Step 1: lem-zl-bertini-finite-field-descent needs only finite type and gives the closed subscheme C_m with base change i(C), so the isomorphism is compatible with the immersions. Step 2: finite type of C_m, via the affine quotient description (Tag 01QO) and finite-type base change. Step 3: Spec k -> Spec k_m is flat, quasi-compact and surjective, and C -> C_m is surjective by base change of surjections. Step 4: smoothness by fpqc descent (Tag 02VL); geometric connectedness by checking over the algebraically closed k (Tag 0387). Step 5: pure dimension one, by Tag 00OT for local dimension 1 on C, then lem-trf-field-extension-component-local-dimension with L=k and then with the identity extension to get every component of dimension 1. Step 6: the residue field kappa(z) embeds in k, so it is algebraic, and lem-kun-closed-point-field (a) gives z closed with finite residue extension. Step 7 is an elementary quantifier step. The route matches paragraph 2 of the main-20261015 proof of thm-zl-real-mixed-by-curves and the last paragraph of the lem-zl-bertini-finite-cover-curve proof. No SGA is cited and there is no cycle. The only citer, lem-zl-two-point-curve-constituent-purity, uses exactly what the statement gives. Batch-5 flag: lem-trf-smooth-fpqc-base-descent is a generic Mathlib-status leaf, and lem-trf-field-extension-component-local-dimension is an unsplit generic Stacks dimension lemma (02FY, 0A21). Neither assumed statement gives these results and neither is a step in proving them, so I accept both citations. Edge cases checked: generic point, empty finite set, nonempty C, nonreduced X_0, and A^1 inside A^2 with unbounded residue degrees. No changes.
